result.question: Work out TDCG for Transformer 1 at MAIN at both the first and the last oil sample between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Add up only hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co, and leave out co2, oxygen and nitrogen. For each of the two samples, give me the timestamp, each gas value and the total. State which IEEE C57.104 condition level each total falls in, using these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630. Then give the change in TDCG in ppm/day between the two samples. If either sample is missing any of the six gases, don't use it. Move to the next earliest or next latest complete sample, and tell me which timestamps you ended up using.
result.answer:
**TDCG for Transformer 1 at MAIN (2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19)**

There were four oil samples in this window. The first and last both had all six gases, so I didn't need to substitute either one. I used 2024-01-15T00:00:00 and 2024-01-18T00:00:00.

| Gas (ppm) | First sample: 2024-01-15T00:00:00 | Last sample: 2024-01-18T00:00:00 |
|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen (H₂) | 2845 | 2900 |
| Methane (CH₄) | 7406 | 7350 |
| Ethane (C₂H₆) | 5467 | 5450 |
| Ethylene (C₂H₄) | 16684 | 16600 |
| Acetylene (C₂H₂) | 7 | 7 |
| CO | 32 | 33 |
| **TDCG** | **32,441** | **32,340** |
| **IEEE C57.104 level** | **Condition 4** (above 4630) | **Condition 4** (above 4630) |

**Change in TDCG:** (32,340 − 32,441) / 3 days = **−33.7 ppm/day**, a slight decrease.

Both totals are about seven times the Condition 4 limit. Ethylene, methane and ethane make up most of the total, while acetylene stays low. That pattern usually points to a high-temperature thermal fault rather than electrical arcing. The small drop over three days doesn't bring the transformer out of Condition 4.
